subject: [PATCH v4 1/3] mm: swap: move LRU insertion out of the swap cache allocator

2026-08-25.patch_summary: This patch moves the insertion of a folio into the LRU (Least Recently Used) list out of the swap cache allocator, allowing callers to decide when to add it to the LRU or free it directly. This change is necessary for zswap writeback, which requires a swap cache folio that can be freed immediately after writeback completes. The patch updates several functions in mm/swap_state.c and mm/zswap.c to reflect this change.

reviews.author: Kunwu Chan
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that the new allocator contract is preserved by all callers of __swap_cache_alloc_folio(), but pointed out a minor consistency issue in swapfile.c referencing the old function name.
reviews.raw_body:
I checked the callers of __swap_cache_alloc_folio(). The regular 
swap-in paths add the folio to the LRU after allocation, while 
the zswap writeback path keeps it off-LRU for the dropbehind 
handling in patch 3. 
The new allocator contract is preserved by all callers.

swapfile.c still references the old name in a comment \u2014 minor
consistency nit.

Reviewed-by: Kunwu Chan <kunwu.chan@gmail.com>

Thanks,
KunWu

2026-09-08.patch_summary: This patch moves the insertion of a folio into the LRU (Least Recently Used) list out of the swap cache allocator. The swap cache allocator is used by zswap writeback to allocate a folio that can be freed directly once writeback completes, without being on the LRU. This change allows for more flexibility in managing swap cache folios and prevents potential issues with synchronous devices or asynchronous ones. The patch updates several files, including mm/swap.h and mm/swap_state.c, to reflect this change.
